ai.cloudConsent.label: Allow cloud AI
ai.cloudConsent.description: Cmdr sends nothing to a cloud AI service until you turn this on.
ai.cloudConsent.intro: With this on, Cmdr sends these to the AI service you set up below:
ai.cloudConsent.whereItGoes: Where your data goes, and what happens to it there, depends on the service you pick and your agreement with it. That includes Ollama, LM Studio, and custom endpoints: the data goes wherever that server runs. Cmdr’s own servers never see any of it.
ai.cloudConsent.folderSuggestions: New folder name suggestions: the current folder’s path and up to 100 names in it
ai.cloudConsent.search: Search in plain words: the text you type
ai.cloudConsent.selection: Select by description: what you type, plus up to 240 names from the current folder
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.title: Ask Cmdr, when you chat or when it starts a conversation on its own:
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.item.names: The names and paths of files and folders Cmdr looks at to answer you
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.item.contents: Parts of files Cmdr opens to answer you: some text, PDF pages, what’s inside an archive, and a photo’s camera details and location
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.item.envelope: What you’re looking at right now: your current folder, cursor, selection, and connected drives
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.item.attachments: Any file or folder you attach to a question, by its name and path only
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.item.memory: The notes Cmdr keeps about you, sent again with every message
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.contentsRule: Cmdr never sends whole files, photos, or thumbnails. When you ask about a file, it can read a limited part of it: some lines of text, a few pages of a PDF along with its title and author, the list of files inside an archive, or a photo’s camera details, including where it was taken. Photo search works the same way: the text Cmdr recognized inside the matching photos and their tags go to your provider so it can find them. Cmdr can suggest renames, moves, and cleanups, and nothing happens to a file until you approve it.
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.memory: Cmdr writes itself notes about you: how you like things organized, what you’ve turned down before, anything you ask it to remember. Those notes ride along with every message you send, for as long as they exist, and they can include text Cmdr recognized inside your photos. You can read them, or wipe them, any time in the Ask Cmdr settings.
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.proactive: Cmdr also watches the folders you use and starts a conversation when it has something to suggest, so messages can reach your provider without you asking first. You can turn that off in the Ask Cmdr settings, under “On its own”.
ai.cloudConsent.askCmdr.chatsStayLocal: Your Ask Cmdr chats stay on your Mac, in a local database you can open and read.
ai.cloudConsent.logsNote: If you turn on LLM call logging in Advanced settings, Cmdr also saves each request and reply to a folder on your Mac. Those logs stay local too, never sent anywhere.
ai.cloudConsent.turnOffAnyTime: Turn this off any time and Cmdr stops sending right away. Your service, key, and chats stay as they are.
